clue.text: Note a foreign article giving the animals of the region

parts.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
un is the French word for a
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone makes a note of a piece in an overseas journal that lists local wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a foreign' and 'article' are separate pieces: the first is the French for 'a', the second is the plain English article.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the term is the zoologist's collective word for the wildlife living in a particular area.

clue.text: River vessel where Flora may be seen

parts.note: a river flows, so crosswords call it a flower
a pot is a vessel for holding things

explanation.surface: A boat on the river where a woman called Flora might be spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River vessel' reads as a boat but splits in two. A river is a thing that flows, a crossword convention, and Flora is plant life, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: flora means plants, and plants are displayed growing in such a container.

clue.text: Piano in university band causing trouble

indicators.note: in tells us the piano letter sits within the university and band pieces

parts.note: a set is a band or group of people
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: The pianist in a student group is the source of some bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places P inside U plus SET. 'causing' simply links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to disturb or distress someone is to bother them.

clue.text: What the vacuum needs to be, if it's to go on working

definitions.text: What the vacuum needs to be, if it's to go on working

parts.words: What the vacuum needs to be, if it's to go on working
parts.note: the vacuum is not a household cleaner but an empty space, which survives only while sealed so that nothing can leak in

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: an empty space stays empty only when perfectly sealed against the atmosphere.

clue.text: Trained and became a doctor

definitions.meaning: to train is to rehearse a skill repeatedly
a qualified doctor who starts work is said to do this in medicine

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one verb: drilled a skill repeatedly, and worked professionally in medicine.

clue.text: Boat carrying a small charge

definitions.meaning: a small flat-bottomed dinghy with a squared-off bow goes by this name
a baby carriage holds an infant, the small charge of whoever pushes it

explanation.surface: A vessel loaded with a modest amount of explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: The charge is not explosive: it is a baby in someone's care. In Britain a baby carriage has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a kind of dinghy, and the British baby carriage that holds an infant.

clue.text: Make hostile soldier, for example, suffer pain

parts.note: a soldier is one caste of ant
to agonise is to suffer great pain or anguish

explanation.surface: Someone forces an unfriendly trooper to endure torment, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make hostile soldier' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after 'hostile'; the soldier is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to provoke enmity in someone is to turn them against you.

clue.text: Vegetable mother has to top and tail

indicators.note: has tells us mother takes the repeated word around her, one copy at each end
top and tail says the word to appears twice, once at the start and once at the end

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum has to trim both ends off a vegetable before cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top and tail' is kitchen talk for trimming both ends of a vegetable; here it says where the repeated word goes, and 'has' makes mother hold a copy at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: botanically a fruit, it is treated in the kitchen as salad produce.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing not wearing' a dress

definitions.meaning: a lazy, aimless person lacking ambition is described this way
a shift is a simple straight dress, so someone without one lacks a shift

explanation.surface: A layabout who has no frock on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a whimsical reading: a shift is a plain dress, so lacking one gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: lazy and aimless, and whimsically lacking a simple frock.

clue.text: Dotheboys' head, stern and gloomy

indicators.note: head picks the leading letter of the school's name

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: The headmaster of Dotheboys Hall, the school in Nicholas Nickleby, is strict and miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes the first letter of Dotheboys; 'stern' is a noun here, the back of a ship. Dotheboys Hall is the grim school in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a poetic adjective for dismal or bleak.

clue.text: No black boy is so attentive

parts.note: O looks like zero, meaning no or none
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
boy was an old term for a male servant

explanation.surface: A remark that a particular lad pays less attention than anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is so' links the wordplay to the definition. 'boy' is used in its dated sense of a male attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone watchful who notices things.

clue.text: Cereal, one planted in a bewildering network

indicators.note: planted in tells us the letter for one is set inside the network word

parts.note: a maze is a confusing network of paths
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grain crop sown within a confusing web of fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted in' puts I inside MAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the grain crop also called corn.

clue.text: Estate settlement given in English translation from Latin

indicators.note: translation from suggests the letters of the next word are rendered into a new form

explanation.surface: A legal document about property, supplied in an English version of the Latin original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation from' looks like language work but signals an anagram of the next word, giving the last five letters. 'given in' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term: a settlement restricting inheritance of land to a fixed line of heirs.

clue.text: Trouble-maker washing one's dirty linen at home

definitions.meaning: someone who stirs up unrest or political dissent

definitions.text: washing one's dirty linen at home
definitions.meaning: the paddle inside a domestic washing machine that stirs the laundry about

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker keeps scandal within the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Washing dirty linen is an idiom for airing scandal; here it is literal, the part of a washing machine that stirs clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a stirrer of unrest, and the device that stirs laundry in a machine.

clue.text: The Tablet, obviously is not this sort of paper

definitions.text: The Tablet, obviously is not this sort of paper

parts.words: The Tablet, obviously is not this sort of paper
parts.note: The Tablet is a British Catholic weekly whose name suggests tabloid, the small newspaper format opposed to the large one

explanation.walkthrough: The Tablet is a British Catholic weekly. Its name hints at 'tabloid', the small format, so it is plainly not the large one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the large-format newspaper is the opposite of a tabloid, which the journal's name suggests.

clue.text: Sock soaked, but too dazed to notice?

parts.note: to sock someone is to punch them
soaked is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone has a wet sock but is too stupefied to realise.
explanation.walkthrough: The sock is a blow, not footwear, and 'soaked' is slang for intoxicated. 'but' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a boxer left stupefied and confused by repeated blows to the head.

clue.text: Quarterstaff discovered by Pooh

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the place Winnie-the-Pooh found on his expedition in A. A. Milne's story

parts.note: the first half, quarter, is a compass direction such as north
the second half, staff, is a pole

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh finds an old wooden fighting stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarterstaff' must be split: quarter is a compass point, staff a long stick. In Milne's book Pooh finds a stick on the 'expotition' and is credited with the discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary allusion: in Milne's book the bear leads an expedition and is credited with finding it.

clue.text: River starting to pollute the sea

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England

indicators.note: starting to takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A waterway begins to contaminate the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting to' takes the first letter of 'pollute'. The Dee is a British river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic synonym: with the definite article it means the ocean.

clue.text: Look with difficulty round a course in fog

indicators.note: round tells us the looking word goes about the other two pieces

parts.note: to peer is to look hard at something difficult to see
soup is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A golfer struggles to see their way about the links in the mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal. The course is part of a meal, not golf. The answer is British slang for dense fog, once notorious in London.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a thick yellowish smog, named after the dish it resembles.

clue.text: Stout Continental with a rising name for musical composition

indicators.note: rising tells us, in a down entry, that the letter for name moves higher up the word

parts.note: stout means fat
an Asian is a person from the continent of Asia

explanation.surface: A portly European with an increasing reputation for writing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' lifts the N from the end of FAT ASIAN up to third place. 'Continental' suggests a European but means anyone from a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a free-form instrumental piece not bound by strict structure.

clue.text: Go for a short walk

definitions.meaning: a go is a player's chance to play in a game
to take a stroll round the garden is to take one of these

explanation.surface: Someone leaves to take a brief stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Two noun senses: a player's chance in a game, and a brief stroll.

clue.text: Little Dorrit's alarm as she cooked for father here

definitions.note: the place the whole clue describes: the debtors' prison where the heroine's father was held in the Dickens novel

indicators.note: cooked suggests the preceding letters are prepared into something new

explanation.surface: Dickens's heroine is frightened while preparing a meal for her father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is the anagram signal for the three words before it. In Dickens's novel Little Dorrit's father is held in this London debtors' prison, where she looks after him, so the whole clue describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary reference: the London debtors' prison where William Dorrit lived in the Dickens novel.

clue.text: Plaintiveness of the page with the musketeer

parts.note: Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers

explanation.surface: The sorrowful air of a servant boy who attends a musketeer.
explanation.walkthrough: The page is a sheet of a book, abbreviated, not a servant. 'of the' and 'with the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a quality that stirs pity or sadness.

clue.text: Note the carriage one gets stiff in, and go through

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

parts.words: the carriage one gets stiff in
parts.note: a hearse is the vehicle that carries a stiff, slang for a corpse

explanation.surface: Observe the cramped coach that leaves passengers aching, then pass along it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one gets stiff in' is a grim joke: a stiff is slang for a corpse, carried in a funeral vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to run over lines or a performance in practice.

clue.text: When short, 22 ac borrowed from share capital

definitions.note: the answer to 22 across can mean to go over again, and this is the abbreviated word for doing that

indicators.note: borrowed from says the letters are taken out of the run of the following words

explanation.surface: A firm short of cash takes money out of its equity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borrowed from' lifts the answer out of 'share capital'. The definition refers to 22 across, which can mean to recite again; the answer is a shortened word for that.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation of recapitulate, meaning to summarise or run over the main points again.

clue.text: Hacks back to firm plaster

indicators.note: back tells us the word for hacks is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Journalists return to a company to apply a hard coating to walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CUTS into STUC, joined 'to' CO. 'Hacks' is a verb, not journalists, and 'firm' is a business, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fine render used for coating walls and moulding decoration.

clue.text: He painted a bird circling the river

indicators.note: circling tells us the bird goes around the letter for river

parts.note: a coot is a black water bird
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An artist made a picture of a bird flying round above a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts COOT around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French landscape artist Jean-Baptiste-Camille, who made many pictures.

clue.text: Enthusiastic singer standing up

indicators.note: standing up tells us, in a down entry, that the word runs from bottom to top

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: A keen vocalist rises to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns DIVA upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: keen or eager.

clue.text: Fate, nonetheless, of the clergy

indicators.note: read as none-the-less, it says the word loses its O, the letter that looks like nothing

parts.note: Clotho is one of the three Fates of Greek myth, the spinner of life's thread

explanation.surface: Such is destiny, even so, for churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' splits into 'none the less': the Greek Fate CLOTHO loses her O, which stands for nothing. 'of' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: with the definite article, it is a collective term for ministers of the church.

clue.text: Hear privately talk of the First Lady's fall

indicators.note: talk of tells us the following phrase is to be spoken rather than read

parts.note: Eve was the first woman, so her fall is Eve's drop

explanation.surface: Someone listens in secret to gossip about the president's wife taking a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talk of' signals a sound-alike of EVE'S DROP. The First Lady is the Bible's first woman, not a president's wife, and her fall also recalls Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to listen secretly to a conversation not meant for you.

clue.text: Urge boss to get a security device

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
a boss is a raised stud or knob, as on a shield

explanation.surface: Someone nags the manager to buy an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The boss is a knob, not a manager, and the 'security device' is a whimsical description of a snap fastener, the British name for which is the answer. 'to get' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a snap fastener holds clothing securely closed.

clue.text: Bill Hill, Thespian

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A man named Bill Hill who works on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The two capitalised words are not a name: each gives a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stage performer.
